$comment: Conformance vectors for X/Twitter weighted character counting. Expected values are derived from the rules x.com's composer applies and stated as arithmetic in each `why`; they are not snapshots of any implementation. See README.md, including how to falsify them.

categories.basic: Plain text in the light ranges. If these fail, nothing else matters.
categories.heavy: Characters outside the light ranges, which cost 2. CJK is the common case and the reason a 200-character Japanese post does not fit.
categories.emoji: The one-emoji-one-unit rule: an emoji in X's table costs 2 however many code points build it. Weighting the code points one at a time is too high on every emoji built from more than one.
categories.url: The flat 23, and where X finds a link: with or without a protocol, on any of the 1,581 endings x.com recognises, stopping before the punctuation that ends a sentence.
categories.not-a-url: Text that must NOT be charged 23: an email address, an ending that is not one, a domain glued to a "#". A spurious 23 sends an author rewriting copy that already fitted.
categories.normalisation: The same visible string must cost the same however it was encoded.
categories.boundary: The exact edges of the published ranges. Off-by-one lives here.
categories.structural: Empty strings, whitespace, and the degenerate inputs that produce a crash rather than a wrong number.

vectors.name: empty
vectors.why: Nothing costs nothing.

vectors.name: single-space
vectors.why: U+0020 is inside 0x0000–0x10FF, so 1.

vectors.name: ascii-hello
vectors.why: Five Latin letters, all weight 1.

vectors.name: ascii-sentence
vectors.text: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
vectors.why: 44 characters, every one inside the first light range.

vectors.name: newlines-count
vectors.why: Line feeds are U+000A — inside the light range, and they are charged, not ignored.

vectors.name: latin-accents-precomposed
vectors.why: U+00E9 is a single code point below 0x1100, so 1 like the rest.

vectors.name: cyrillic
vectors.why: Cyrillic sits at U+0400–U+04FF, inside the first light range. Weight 1, which surprises people who assume "non-Latin means 2".

vectors.name: hebrew
vectors.why: U+05D0–U+05EA, inside the first light range.

vectors.name: thai
vectors.why: Thai is U+0E00–U+0E7F, inside the light range. Six code points, six units — note this is more than the four grapheme clusters a reader sees.

vectors.name: japanese
vectors.why: Five kana at U+3053 upward, all above 0x10FF, so 2 each.

vectors.name: chinese
vectors.why: Four CJK ideographs, 2 each.

vectors.name: korean
vectors.why: Five precomposed Hangul syllables at U+AC00 upward, 2 each.

vectors.name: mixed-latin-cjk
vectors.why: 5 Latin (5) + 1 space (1) + 5 kana at 2 (10) = 16.

vectors.name: emoji-simple
vectors.why: One emoji, weight 2. Also the case everyone already passes.

vectors.name: emoji-with-variation-selector
vectors.why: U+2764 plus U+FE0F. Two code points, ONE emoji, so 2. Weighted one code point at a time it is 2 + 2 = 4.

vectors.name: emoji-skin-tone
vectors.why: Thumbs up plus a skin-tone modifier is one emoji at 2, not two emoji at 4.

vectors.name: emoji-flag
vectors.why: Two regional indicators forming one flag: 2, not 4. A per-code-point counter reports 4.

vectors.name: emoji-zwj-mechanic
vectors.why: Person + ZWJ + wrench = one emoji at 2. Per code point it is 200+100+200 = 5 after dividing by scale, and 5 is the number reported in twitter-text#369.

vectors.name: emoji-newer-than-the-published-table
vectors.why: Bird + ZWJ + black large square is the black bird, from Emoji 15.0, and x.com charges it as one emoji: 2. The last emoji table X published, twemoji-parser 14.0.0 from 2022, does not know it, so a counter built on that table charges the pieces: 2 + 1 + 2 = 5.

vectors.name: emoji-zwj-family
vectors.why: Four people joined by three ZWJs — seven code points, one emoji, 2. Per code point it is (200*4 + 100*3)/100 = 11. If you get 11, you fell through to the per-code-point path. If you get 7, you counted code points and forgot the weights. If you get 11 in Python, `len()` gave you 7 and something else went wrong too.

vectors.name: emoji-two-adjacent
vectors.why: Two separate emoji, 2 each. Guards against a cluster walker that swallows neighbours.

vectors.name: emoji-in-prose
vectors.why: "ship it " is 8 at weight 1, plus one emoji at 2.

vectors.name: emoji-keycap
vectors.why: Digit + U+FE0F + U+20E3 is one keycap emoji at 2, not three units.

vectors.name: emoji-keycap-without-selector
vectors.why: Digit + U+20E3 with no U+FE0F between them is still the keycap emoji at 2. Counted apart they are 1 + 2 = 3.

vectors.name: emoji-joined-but-not-a-sequence
vectors.why: A joiner between two emoji that do not form a known sequence joins nothing: 2 + 1 + 2 = 5. One unit at 2 is only for sequences in the emoji table.

vectors.name: url-https-short
vectors.why: Flat 23 regardless of length — 13 characters charged as 23. Links can cost MORE than they are long.

vectors.name: url-https-long
vectors.why: Same flat 23. 65 characters charged as 23.

vectors.name: url-www-no-scheme
vectors.why: A www. host with no scheme is still linkified.

vectors.name: url-bare-domain
vectors.why: THE ONE THAT UNDERCOUNTS. No scheme, no www., still a link, still 23. A matcher requiring http(s):// or www. reports 11 and tells the author a post fits that the API will reject.

vectors.name: url-bare-domain-with-path
vectors.why: The path is part of the link, so still one 23 rather than 23 plus the path.

vectors.name: url-in-prose
vectors.why: "read this: " is 11 characters at weight 1, the link is a flat 23, and " now" is 4. 11 + 23 + 4 = 38. The text either side of a link must keep its own weighting.

vectors.name: url-adjacent-to-cjk
vectors.why: 5 kana at 2 (10) + 1 space + 23 = 34. Checks that the link split does not lose the weighting of the text around it.

vectors.name: url-then-full-stop
vectors.why: "Read more: " is 11, the link is a flat 23, and the full stop is 1: 35. A path may not END on a full stop, so the stop belongs to the sentence. A matcher that runs to the next space takes it into the link and reports 34: one short, whenever a sentence ends with a link.

vectors.name: url-then-comma
vectors.why: "See " is 4, the link is 23, and ", then reply" is 12: 39. The comma is not part of the link.

vectors.name: url-in-brackets
vectors.why: 1 + 23 + 1 = 25. The closing bracket has no opening one inside the link, so it stays outside.

vectors.name: url-then-question-mark
vectors.why: "Is it " is 6, the link is 23, the question mark is 1: 30. A query needs something after its "?", so a bare one ends the sentence, not the link.

vectors.name: url-brackets-inside-the-path
vectors.why: Brackets that open and close inside the path are part of it, which is what keeps a Wikipedia link whole. One link, 23.

vectors.name: url-full-stop-is-the-281st
vectors.why: 256 + 1 space + 23 + 1 full stop = 281, one over the limit. A counter that takes the stop into the link says 280 and calls this postable. This is the vector that costs somebody a rejected post.

vectors.name: url-markdown-ending-with-protocol
vectors.why: With a protocol, .md is an ending like any other (it is the country ending of Moldova), so this is a link at 23. The exception x.com makes for .md applies to bare domains only. Compare not-a-url-markdown-file.

vectors.name: url-ending-newer-than-the-published-list
vectors.why: .music is one of seven endings x.com recognises that are missing from the list X published in twitter-text, so this bare domain is a link at 23. A counter that uses the published list sees thirteen ordinary characters and reports 13.

vectors.name: url-government-ending
vectors.why: A bare domain on an ending outside the handful everyone remembers. x.com recognises 1,581 of them; a counter with a short list of its own reports 14.

vectors.name: url-missing-space-makes-a-link
vectors.why: "the " is 4, "end.Next" is a link at 23 because .next is a generic ending and case does not matter, and " sentence" is 9: 36. A missing space after a full stop can manufacture a link.

vectors.name: url-upper-case
vectors.why: Link matching ignores case, so capitals change nothing: 23.

vectors.name: url-non-latin-with-protocol
vectors.why: With a protocol, a domain in any script is a link: .рф is the Cyrillic country ending of Russia. 23. Compare not-a-url-non-latin-bare.

vectors.name: url-bare-domain-query-left-out
vectors.why: Without a protocol a query is only kept when a path comes before it. Here the link is example.com at 23 and "?q=1" is 4 more: 27. With https:// in front the whole string is one link at 23.

vectors.name: not-a-url-eg
vectors.why: "e.g." is not a link. Charging it 23 would report 37 for an 18-unit sentence and send an author rewriting copy that fits.

vectors.name: not-a-url-filename
vectors.why: .js is not a domain ending, so this is 24 plain characters. A counter matching any dotted token charges 23 for the filename. Compare not-a-url-markdown-file, where .md is an ending and the file name is still not charged as a link.

vectors.name: not-a-url-markdown-file
vectors.why: "I updated " is 10 and README.md is 9 ordinary characters: 19. .md is the country ending of Moldova, and X's published library makes README.md a link at 23, but x.com does not: there a bare domain ending in .md is a file name, not a link. With https:// in front it is a link again; see url-markdown-ending-with-protocol.

vectors.name: not-a-url-version
vectors.why: Neither "78" nor "0" is a domain ending, so a version string is 22 ordinary characters.

vectors.name: not-a-url-sentence-end
vectors.why: "then" is not a domain ending, so the missing space manufactures nothing and this is 24 characters. That is luck rather than a rule: see url-missing-space-makes-a-link.

vectors.name: not-a-url-almost-tld
vectors.why: .coma is not a domain ending, so this is twelve ordinary characters — which means "example.com" costs 23 and "example.coma" costs 12, and ADDING a character made the post cheaper. Surprising, correct, and the clearest demonstration that link detection is decided on the whole token rather than incrementally.

vectors.name: not-a-url-ellipsis
vectors.why: Consecutive dots are not a hostname.

vectors.name: not-a-url-email
vectors.why: A domain straight after "@" is not a link, so the address is 16 ordinary characters: 5 + 16 + 6 = 27. Charging the domain 23 reports 39 and tells an author a post that fits is too long.

vectors.name: not-a-url-after-hash
vectors.why: A domain straight after "#" is not a link. The same goes for "$", "@", a letter or a digit. Twelve characters, 12.

vectors.name: not-a-url-no-ending
vectors.why: A protocol is not enough: the host must finish with a recognised ending, and localhost has none. 21 characters, 21.

vectors.name: not-a-url-other-scheme
vectors.why: Only http and https start a link, and a bare domain may not directly follow a slash, so nothing here is one. 17 characters, 17.

vectors.name: not-a-url-www-without-ending
vectors.why: "www." does not make a link; a recognised ending does, and "example" is not one. Eleven characters, 11.

vectors.name: not-a-url-label-too-long
vectors.why: One part of a domain may be at most 63 characters. This one is 64, so the whole string is 68 ordinary characters. At 63 it would be a link at 23.

vectors.name: not-a-url-underscore-in-the-name
vectors.why: An underscore is allowed in a subdomain but not in the name next to the ending, and a bare domain may not start straight after one, so neither "my_site.io" nor "site.io" is a link. Ten characters, 10.

vectors.name: not-a-url-non-latin-bare
vectors.why: Without a protocol only an ASCII domain is linked. Eight Cyrillic letters and a dot, all at weight 1: 9. Compare url-non-latin-with-protocol.

vectors.name: nfc-decomposed-accent
vectors.why: "cafe" + U+0301 combining acute normalises under NFC to "café", four code points at weight 1. Without normalisation this is 5, so the same visible word costs differently depending on which editor produced it.

vectors.name: nfc-korean-decomposed
vectors.why: Two conjoining jamo normalise under NFC to the single syllable 가 (U+AC00), which is above 0x10FF and so costs 2. Unnormalised, the jamo are also above 0x10FF and would cost 4.

vectors.name: boundary-last-light-char
vectors.why: U+10FF is the last code point of the first light range. Inclusive, so 1.

vectors.name: boundary-first-heavy-char
vectors.why: U+1100 is one past the range. 2. Together with the previous case this pins the edge in both directions.

vectors.name: boundary-general-punctuation-start
vectors.why: U+2000 opens the second light range.

vectors.name: boundary-zwj-alone
vectors.why: A bare ZWJ is the last code point of the second range, weight 1. This is the value that makes the family emoji 11 rather than 14 when counted wrongly, so it is worth pinning on its own.

vectors.name: boundary-just-past-second-range
vectors.why: U+200E, the left-to-right mark, is one past the second range and costs 2. Invisible and expensive.

vectors.name: boundary-en-dash
vectors.why: U+2013 is inside 0x2010–0x201F. Dashes and smart quotes are cheap; that is the point of the third range.

vectors.name: boundary-prime
vectors.why: U+2032 opens the fourth range, 0x2032–0x2037.

vectors.name: boundary-just-past-fourth-range
vectors.why: One past the last light range.

vectors.name: exactly-280-ascii
vectors.why: The limit itself. Fits — the comparison is <=, not <.

vectors.name: over-by-one
vectors.why: One over. The two cases together pin which way the boundary falls.

vectors.name: cjk-140-fills-280
vectors.text: 漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢漢
vectors.why: 140 ideographs at 2 each is exactly the limit — the arithmetic behind "a Japanese post gets half as many characters".
